# What Next {#what-next}

## How to see more? {#see-more}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
{{< nh-video source-emerges variant="film-en" class="slide-video media-height-lg" style="--media-max-height: 580px;" controls=true muted=true playsinline=true preload="metadata" poster="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/sensitivity/source_emerges_en.jpg" aria-label="Simulated neutrinos accumulate around an invented point source; the significance grows with exposure and depends on how accurately the directions are measured." >}}
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
- The source emerges from the background gradually, year after year.
- **Larger volume:** more events.
- **Sharper directions:** less background around the source.
- The significance grows as the square root of the exposure and is inversely proportional to the angular error.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
Illustration: an invented source of NGC 1068's strength, simulated events, computed significance · not a forecast for any detector.
:::

### IceCube-Gen2

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**South Pole, ice**

- IceCube: 1 km³, operating.
- Upgrade: 5 new strings, installed in 2026.
- Gen2: 8 km³ optical array, proposed.
:::
::: {.column width="61%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/observatories/icecube-gen2-layout.png){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 560px;" fig-alt="The proposed IceCube-Gen2 expansion."}

::: {.media-caption}
[Gen2 design illustration. DESY, Science Communication Lab.](https://icecube-gen2.wisc.edu/facility/detectors/)
:::
:::
:::::

### KM3NeT

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**Mediterranean Sea**

- ARCA: about 1 km³ for neutrino astronomy.
- ORCA: for neutrino oscillations.
- Under construction and already taking data.
:::
::: {.column width="61%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/observatories/km3net-artist-impression.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 560px;" fig-alt="Artist's impression of a KM3NeT building block on the sea floor."}

::: {.media-caption}
Artist's impression · [Edward Berbee/Nikhef · KM3NeT](https://www.km3net.org/pictures-and-videos/picture-galleries/album-artists-impressions/)
:::
:::
:::::

### Baikal-GVD

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**Lake Baikal, fresh water**

- 2026: 16 clusters, operating.
- Effective volume about 0.8 km³.
- Grows every winter: new clusters are deployed from the ice.
:::
::: {.column width="61%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/observatories/baikal-gvd-2026.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 560px; --media-bg: #fff;" fig-alt="The 2026 configuration of Baikal-GVD: sixteen clusters."}

::: {.media-caption}
[2026 configuration. Baikal-GVD.](https://baikal-gvd.jinr.ru/telescope)
:::
:::
:::::

### TRIDENT

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**South China Sea**

- Design: 7.5 km³, 1211 strings.
- Hybrid modules: PMTs and silicon photomultipliers.
- R&D and a pathfinder programme.
:::
::: {.column width="61%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/observatories/trident-layout.png){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 540px;" fig-alt="The proposed TRIDENT layout."}

::: {.media-caption}
[Proposed layout. Ye et al., Nature Astronomy (2023), Fig. 2.](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-023-02087-6)
:::
:::
:::::

### NEON

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
**South China Sea**

- Design: 10 km³, 1200 strings.
- Multi-PMT modules.
- Proposal and hardware R&D.
:::
::: {.column width="61%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/observatories/neon-layout.png){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 540px;" fig-alt="The proposed NEON layout."}

::: {.media-caption}
[Proposed layout. Zhang et al., Fig. 3.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.05122)
:::
:::
:::::

### HUNT

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="47%"}
**China + Russia · about 30 km³ · 20-inch PMTs**

- The ice is a platform: strings are deployed from the frozen lake every winter.
- In water light scatters less than in ice, so cascade directions are sharper.
- A northern site: the Galactic Centre is below the horizon 75% of the day.
- A gamma-ray partner: LHAASO watches the same northern sky.
:::
::: {.column width="49%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/observatories/hunt-design.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 520px;" fig-alt="Design illustration of HUNT."}

::: {.media-caption}
[HUNT / IHEP, CAS](https://ihep.cas.cn/astro/en/research/sf/ucp/202510/t20251011_7986821.html)
:::
:::
:::::

## What do we want to discover? {#what-to-discover}

![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/prospects/discovery-map.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 600px;" fig-alt="Open questions on the neutrino-energy axis over the measured spectrum of cosmic neutrinos."}

::: {.media-caption}
Questions on the energy axis · spectrum: [IceCube (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22233v3) · [Glashow resonance: IceCube (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15051) · [KM3-230213A: KM3NeT (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08543-1)
:::

## Where are the sources? {#where-are-the-sources}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="64%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/prospects/sources-sky.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 400px;" fig-alt="Sky map: the Milky Way, NGC 1068, TXS 0506+056 and KM3-230213A."}

::: {.question}
- **Then what?** Cosmic accelerators: protons of tens of PeV and more.
- **And where?** Our Galaxy, NGC 1068, a blazar candidate, and a crowd of faint sources still to resolve.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
**Found:**

- our Galaxy;
- NGC 1068 and other Seyfert galaxies;
- blazar candidates.

**Still unclear:**

- where most of the flux comes from.

**Next:**

- bigger telescopes and networks: B-HUNT, KM3NeT, IceCube-Gen2.
:::
:::::

## Who will do it? {#who}

![](media/figures/people-chain.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 300px;" fig-alt="A chain: programme, people, results, the next experiment."}

- Telescopes are built and understood by people.
- The next ones are being built close to you: in the South China Sea (TRIDENT, NEON) and at Lake Baikal, by Russia and China together (B-HUNT).

::: {.takeaway}
- Will there be new discoveries? Of course!
- The only question is who will make them.
:::

## The Textbook {#qft-book}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
![](media/figures/qft-book-cover-en.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 640px;" fig-alt="Front cover of Quantum Field Theory for Experimentalists and Beyond by Dmitry Naumov, volume 1."}

::: {.column width="62%"}
::::: {style="font-size: 34px;"}
**Quantum Field Theory for Experimentalists and Beyond**

A practical course with examples, problems, and solutions: from the foundations to renormalization, anomalies and functional integrals, always tied to experiment.

- In English: three volumes, electronic edition, November 2026.
- In Russian: two volumes, IKI, 2026.
